name: White nationalism
summary: White nationalism holds that white people form a race and nation whose survival, culture and political and demographic dominance should be secured, usually through white-majority or all-white states and sharply restricted non-white immigration. Adherents treat racial differences as largely innate, reject racial equality as a goal and often claim that elites are engineering white decline. Leading figures present it as separation rather than supremacy, which critics dispute, and its economic and religious views vary widely.
scope: The mainstream of the self-described white nationalist movement as represented by Jared Taylor and American Renaissance, with Greg Johnson, Richard Spencer and the Fourteen Words milieu as reference points. It does not cover white supremacy as a wider doctrine (a separate profile), nor civic or non-racial nationalisms that critics label white nationalist. Taylor's White Identity (2011) is the primary text; economic and religious positions are largely unsettled and answered low.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Welfare provision is viewed as failed and as shared with non-whites; inferred, and strands differ on economics.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The movement has no common economic line; some strands are populist, others market-oriented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic views range from libertarian to anti-capitalist across strands, so there is no shared answer.

public-ownership.rationale: Not a theme of the movement; inferred opposition from its general hostility to the state expanding for non-racial ends.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No shared position; the movement's economic strands split.

unions-good.rationale: Economics is secondary to race and strands differ on labor.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not a defining issue; some strands are libertarian, others reject it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Some strands attack corporations as multicultural, others favor free enterprise.

cut-welfare.rationale: Taylor treats welfare as having failed to fix black and Hispanic poverty, and American Renaissance ties welfare to birth rates.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred rejection of socialist forms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents favor border and security control but also fear state surveillance of themselves.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Taylor frames his case as free speech and sued over suspension; adherents see hate-speech law as aimed at them.

strong-leader.rationale: Some strands, notably the alt-right, favor strong leadership; others stress representative government.

state-harmful.rationale: The program requires a state to secure a racial homeland and borders, so the state is not seen as harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the American strands' general right-wing positions and self-defense concerns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law-and-order stance linked to crime claims about minorities; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Taylor wants legal means to preserve local majorities, which implies local control.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on crime and law and order.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents stress white birth rates and families, and the Fourteen Words speak of a future for white children.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Most adherents oppose it though some, such as Greg Johnson, urge tolerance of gay members.

abortion-legal.rationale: Many leading figures oppose abortion because of falling white birth rates, but some, such as Spencer, accept it on eugenic grounds, so the movement is split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents hold varied faiths, including atheism and paganism, so there is no shared line.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Taylor treats racial preferences for blacks and Hispanics as unfair to whites and too entrenched for legislatures to abolish, though he never sets out a call to end them; opposing race-conscious remedies follows from the movement's focus on white interests.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from biological-determinist view of race and sex.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Culture is held to be a product of race and white culture should be foremost in white-majority countries.

gradual-change.rationale: Taylor presents himself as moderate while others seek radical change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Taylor says immigration should be cut close to zero and restricted to Europeans in most American strands.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents defend national and racial sovereignty and distrust global bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Economics is not defining and strands differ.

nation-first.rationale: Interests of the white nation or race come first, though pan-white solidarity cuts across it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and hostility to universalist human-rights politics.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders are the opposite of the demand to keep white majorities.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed in core texts, and environmental views vary among adherents.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from general right-wing skepticism of state-led programs.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Adherents hold no common position on this question.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Prominent figures stress peaceful, metapolitical change, though violent strands exist.

experts-over-public.rationale: Adherents distrust academic experts yet cite race science.

land-value-tax.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from family and heritage emphasis.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism is common among strands, but not universal.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Never advocated; inferred from rejection of communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Some antisemitic strands attack banks, mainstream strands do not address it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: This is not a common theme in the movement's writings.

one-party-rule.rationale: Taylor names representative government as a European principle to preserve.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Taylor values representative government, but democracy is not defended when it produces demographic change.

direct-votes.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from rejection of the left.

right-to-secede.rationale: Racial partition of territory is proposed by some figures, which implies secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Racial hierarchy beliefs imply this for supremacist strands; separatist strands deny rule over others.

political-violence-never.rationale: Leading figures disavow violence, but the milieu includes terrorism and the Fourteen Words.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Only Christian Identity strands favor it; most do not.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from need for a state to secure borders.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The defining aim is a state, or states, made up of one race or ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Ethnic conflict, not class, is held to drive history; Taylor says history is the history of warfare.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Racial gaps are attributed to innate differences, so equal outcomes are rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Ethnonationalist logic grants homelands to each people, though it is not stated for this case.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents reject racial redress and treat Western civilization as a benefit.

civilizational-union.rationale: White nationalism is a pan-nationalism that unites whites across states.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Group interest is affirmed, individual self-interest is not a doctrinal point.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Adherents hold no common position on this question.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Pronatalist for whites, though some want others' growth limited.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Western civilization is treated as an achievement to preserve.

human-enhancement.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Deplatformed and surveilled dissidents have reason to favor private communication; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Taylor wants America to remain a European-majority nation.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism is common but not defining.

population-transfer.rationale: Some adherents back remigration and Spencer called for "peaceful ethnic cleansing", while others reject it, so the movement is split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Leading figures disavow violence but the movement contemplates coercive separation and includes violent strands.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist and group-conflict themes recur; Taylor says history is warfare.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents see such bans as targeting them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from criticism of welfare dependence.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The movement's core texts do not address this question, so no position can be inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Adherents blame group traits and welfare-driven birth rates rather than population as such.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Taylor argues diversity is a source of conflict, not strength, and that multiracial societies are doomed to failure.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not an issue the movement addresses; inferred from its hierarchical, elite-minded outlook (Taylor argues for selection of leaders by merit and racial interest, not chance).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Adherents see the state as hostile to whites and distrust its powers, yet back harsh measures against perceived enemies; no common line, inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The movement has no common economic line; some strands are populist and others market-oriented.

party-controls-media.rationale: Adherents complain of media control by hostile elites and demand free expression for themselves, so state control is not a goal; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: No doctrine on party command of the army; the movement is mostly non-state and favors a racially defined state, not party control of forces; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the movement's wish to restrict non-white immigration and its view of citizenship as membership of a racial nation; naturalization rules are not discussed.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled in the movement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Organizations differ and the main texts do not address party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The movement is nation- and race-first and generally rejects the EU as a vehicle of mass immigration, though some favour pan-European white unity.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from the admiration among some adherents for strong-leader and authoritarian models; the mainstream does not state it.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religious views vary widely across the movement.

clerical-rule.rationale: Most adherents are secular or Christian and prize racial community over clerical authority; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalist loyalty suggests backing one's own country, though some adherents oppose wars as not serving white interests.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents are split: some want cultural standards, but many present themselves as victims of censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The movement has no settled view on executive term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: The movement has no settled view on recall of officials.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents split between isolationists and those who want white-world solidarity; the movement states no alliance doctrine.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Private property is not an issue for the movement and a state-imposed ownership scheme is not part of its program; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Gun rights are popular in the American milieu, but no doctrine of replacing the army is stated; adherents are split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural, rooted white communities are idealised against multiracial cities, but this is inferred from its homeland rhetoric.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-European and white-homeland thinking favors reuniting ethnic nations, though the issue is rarely addressed directly; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hostility to academic and media elites as hostile to white interests is common, though inferred rather than stated as doctrine.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Taylor holds that races differ innately in ability and that civilizations differ in achievement, rejecting equality of groups.

death-penalty.rationale: Adherents generally favor tough punishment, but the death penalty is not a defining position; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The movement opposes gender-equality curricula as part of cultural decline, but sex education itself is not a stated issue; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Adherents split between religious and secular or pagan strands and the movement has no school-curriculum line.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Traditionalist strands favor restriction, and some link porn to Jewish influence, but others are libertarian; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the goal of a white homeland defined by ancestry; birthright citizenship is not discussed in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Support for minority languages is tied to multiculturalism, which Taylor opposes; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for minority religions would cut against a unified white national identity; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The movement stresses racial solidarity and conformity to the group's identity over individualist nonconformity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: No common line; some oppose transfers to the non-white world, others blame global finance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of racial-national sovereignty over any economic system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The movement has no stated view on how constitutions should be remade; strands differ.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Strands differ; some favour authoritarian means for racial ends, others stress free speech.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the view that duties are owed to the white nation, not to the world's poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the stress on white-majority state sovereignty and self-reliance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: No common line on how the head of state is chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: No common line; some strands blame bankers and others favour markets.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the claim to defend the homeland of white nations against loss of territory and demographic change.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Economic views vary widely, as the audit scope notes.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The USSR's economic character is not a movement issue; strands differ.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from distrust of elites and global regulatory bodies; the movement has no settled environmental stance.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from hostility to international commitments, though some adherents favour a white-nation alliance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: territory matters mainly for ethnic composition, so annexation views depend on who lives there.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: religion is largely unsettled, but white nationalists mostly value church independence.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: they want a head of state who is a champion of white interests, not a neutral figure.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred: they claim separation for white homelands, so forcing unwilling regions to stay is rejected.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the call for racial separation and autonomous white regions or states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: sacred divine rulers are not part of Taylor's secular race-realist program.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Economics is largely unsettled in the movement and adherents are split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Taylor holds that racial differences are largely innate and not erased by environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from distrust of present legal order, though no doctrine on rulers and law exists.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: some figures, such as Spencer, praise expansion as a white destiny, but it is not central.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from the preference for homogeneous national leadership over balanced rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: leader glorification is not a defined position and adherents are split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Never addressed; adherents have no clear position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from a racial rather than class view of history and opposition to Marxism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Never a core question; economic positions are largely unsettled and expropriation is generally disfavoured.

refugee-return.rationale: Never a settled question; adherents' views on refugees' right of return are unrecorded.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the ethnostate and pan-European ideas, where nationality or race, not borders, defines the political unit.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a racial rather than religious basis of identity.

women-must-cover.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the same basis and the movement's hostility to Islam.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from nationalism and hostility to supranational elites.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Some leaders such as Spencer argue for white unity across borders, but this is not the mainstream position.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement seeks its own states or separation rather than minority self-government within a multiracial state; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Taylor and others favour separate homelands over integration; inferred from this stress on separation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The movement treats racial differences as largely innate and sees ideas and culture as secondary; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled, so no inference is made.

no-bailouts.rationale: Economic positions are largely unsettled, so no inference is made.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Adherents oppose anti-discrimination law and judicial enforcement of equality against majority wishes; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Adherents reject racial equality as a goal and oppose mandated representation; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and restricted immigration, but economic views vary widely.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from nationalist scepticism of international agreements; economic views vary.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred; economic and social views are unsettled but the stress on innate differences cuts against it.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Leading figures such as Taylor present the cause as peaceful; inferred, with some milieu dissent.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed; views differ between egalitarian and aristocratic wings.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Adherents want European-descended heritage at the centre of teaching; inferred from the movement's focus on white identity and culture.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Some leading figures criticise consumer materialism and liberal modernity; not central.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Adherents generally favour non-intervention abroad; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Adherents generally oppose foreign military adventures and favour national self-determination; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Adherents blame cultural and media elites more than business, and some strands are pro-market while others attack finance; inferred, so split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist aim of keeping institutions under the national (white) community's control and the claim that outside elites drive white decline.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: White nationalists treat low white birth rates as a core threat and prefer higher births to immigration; state incentives specifically are inferred, as no cited source proposes them.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the aim of preserving white-majority communities and homelands; not a stated policy in Taylor's work.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic views are unsettled across the movement, from welfare for whites to free-market positions; the issue is not addressed directly.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from rejection of universalist democracy promotion and the view that diverse societies, not regime type, determine conflict.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents split between law-and-order nationalists and those who see the present legal order as illegitimate; no settled position.

non-intervention.rationale: Many white nationalists oppose foreign wars and nation-building, though some back intervention for white or Western interests; inferred and mixed.

industrial-unions.rationale: Labor organization is peripheral to the movement; inferred indifference, with no settled view on union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The replacement narrative blames a Jewish-led elite for white decline, but Taylor and others decline the Jewish question, so strands are split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on family and white reproduction; legal marriage is not discussed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust government and media but have no stated view on a right to government information.

local-production.rationale: Some strands favor economic nationalism and localism, others market positions; not a defining issue, so split.

informal-organisation.rationale: The mainstream builds organizations, conferences and publications such as American Renaissance, though online informal networks are also common; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on national sovereignty and its rejection of international constraints on immigration; international law is not discussed.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by race, not faith; religion is left to individuals and strands range from Christian to pagan to secular.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist separatism: it seeks sovereign homelands, not ritual submission to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Economic views are unsettled in the movement and the sources give no position on regional fiscal transfers; inferred as split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: adherents defend private property and reject common ownership of the means of production, though economics varies.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to Marxism and class-struggle thinking; communism is generally treated as an enemy, not documented as a core plank.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Sources address welfare only as limited to whites; public service delivery models are unsettled among adherents.

religion-illusion.rationale: Adherents are split between secular and Christian or pagan identity, but few accept the Marxist claim that religion fades with material progress; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Economic questions are largely unsettled in the movement, so no stance on capitalism as a historical stage is documented; inferred as split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Adherents hold innate group differences and traditional sex roles and reject structural patriarchy, so they would not tie equality to economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on traditional family and distinct gender roles, which favours private family care over public provision.

purge-loanwords.rationale: No documented position on loanwords; its cultural nationalism points one way but the issue is marginal. Inferred as split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; its separatist aims and its support for indigenous land authority in other audits pull in different directions. Inferred as split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mainstream white nationalism wants nation-states or ethnostates, not communal property; small intentional-community separatists are a fringe. Inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its ethnostate goal of securing territory for the white nation, which favours settlement that cements white presence.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Many adherents describe a third way beyond both capitalism and communism, but economics is unsettled in the movement; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: white nationalists claim European-descended peoples have a rightful homeland in Europe and North America, but the sources do not discuss priority claims over other residents directly.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Adherents are split: figures such as Jared Taylor distance themselves from outright denial while parts of the wider milieu embrace it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Adherents differ; the sources describe traditional-family conservatism in much of the movement but no settled demand to criminalise same-sex relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: leading figures present themselves as victims of censorship and demand free speech for white identity, though they also favour strong order within their ethnostate.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religious views in the movement vary widely, and the sources give no demand for state punishment of blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: Taylor and others oppose ruling or settling non-white peoples' lands and favour racial separation rather than colonial exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the movement is hostile to Islam and Muslim immigration, so it would not endorse a religious duty of resistance, but it does not address the doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the movement is racial rather than religious in its source of legitimacy and does not address removal of rulers on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: the movement's elite-replacement narrative stresses distrust of existing institutions, but it favours white-majority control over broad direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Taylor and the movement reject racial equality as a goal and deny that racism or privilege structures explain disparities.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditional family and gender-role views; the sources do not discuss gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: The sources do not address assisted dying and adherents' views vary with their religious positions.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: white nationalists see themselves as an identitarian right defined by race, and the movement does not treat left and right as obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the movement's economic views are unsettled, but it rejects the Marxist framework in which this claim sits.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement frames its case in terms of race rather than religion, but reference accounts note anti-Muslim immigration restriction, so agreement is inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Religious views in the movement vary from Christian Identity to paganism and atheism, so there is no shared position.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the movement's hostility to Islam and Muslim presence points toward bans on Muslim dress in state institutions, though no source states this.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The issue is outside the movement's core concerns and adherents' economic views are unsettled.

social-market-economy.rationale: The sources describe the movement's economic views as widely varied, with welfare supported for citizens in some strands and cut in others.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The movement stresses national survival, military strength and homeland defence, so abolishing armed forces runs against its core.

rich-first.rationale: The sources report no settled stance on this development principle, and economic views vary in the movement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: Taylor-style white nationalists often oppose foreign entanglements and favour national self-determination, but the sources do not state a position on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Mainstream white nationalism is oriented to the racial nation and republican or ethnostate forms; hereditary leader succession is not a defining issue, so this is inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Economic views are largely unsettled in the movement (as the scope notes); inferred weakly from its racial rather than cooperative-economic focus.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to globalism and international institutions and its stress on national sovereignty.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement's franchise criterion is race, not property; property qualifications are not part of its programme.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses innate sex and race differences and rejects feminist and ecological-egalitarian frames.

reification.rationale: A Marxist analysis of capitalism that the movement rejects; it attributes social ills to race and elites, not to reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Adherents commonly claim media and finance elites hostile to white interests control the press; inferred at low confidence as agreement with the claim's thrust.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from its desire for stable nation-state institutions; the sources do not address rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: White nationalists want white-majority or all-white states, which implies political membership for whites, but Taylor's separatism is not documented as a call to disenfranchise, so this is inferred.

online-participation.rationale: The movement relies heavily on the internet for organising; its view of online political participation is inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-elite distrust of government; the sources do not address open data.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Its marriage restrictions are racial, not religious; religious intermarriage rules are not part of its mainstream.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Adherents are split: antisemitic strands favour such boycotts, while the mainstream presenting itself as separation not supremacy avoids them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: No stated position; inferred from the movement's distrust of mass deliberation and its focus on racial rather than procedural reform of government.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the movement mostly treats religion as heritage to preserve, though strands (Christian traditionalist, pagan, secular) differ.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement has no common line; some strands are anti-elite and distrust concentrated wealth, others are market-oriented; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Taylor-style writers stress cohesion and traditional norms and mostly oppose open gay service; inferred and not a defining issue.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement defends European heritage and Christianity or cultural traditions, not state atheism; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The movement stresses law and order and ethnic security; abolition of policing is foreign to it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement seeks racially homogeneous states rather than shared rule among communities in one state, inferred from its separatist aim.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Many strands criticize state welfare as shared with non-whites and favour private or kin-based support; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The movement has no common stance on term limits; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Delegable voting is not discussed; the movement is mostly anti-liberal and sceptical of mass democracy, inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Fertility and demographic decline are central worries, but extinction-risk policy is not addressed; inferred as neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Traditional gender roles are common in the milieu, but strands differ and the issue is not defining; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Traditionalist strands favour male headship, though others do not address it; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the view that political voice belongs to the white national community; local votes are not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Not a topic the sources address; inferred from the movement's general suspicion of state intervention that benefits non-white populations, though economic views vary.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the movement's mostly pro-property and pro-market tendencies, and strands differ.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The sources do not address uniformed youth movements; some milieus admire them and the mainstream does not take a position.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the movement has no settled position on nuclear basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to perceived elite and 'globalist' control and its stress on national self-determination; not stated as a platform item.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the movement treats claims of its own people's 'genocide' as central but is hostile to the moral-guilt narratives that formal recognition of others' genocides feeds.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Economic views are largely unsettled across white nationalist strands, ranging from market to welfare positions.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from an ethic of racial survival and defence of the in-group that does not treat killing in self-defence as wrong.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on a deep common European ancestry and heritage.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the movement's view that human differences are innate and biological; sex is not discussed directly.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to feminism and its stress on fixed biological categories; not a topic the sources discuss.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from a milieu that celebrates fallen activists and figures of the movement; not a documented mainstream position.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Religious views vary widely, from Christian Identity to paganism to secularism, so adherents are split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the goal of a white state gathering the people rather than a cultural centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Leading writers stress metapolitics and shifting racial consciousness before political power; inferred and contested among strands.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious views vary widely across the movement and the sources do not address how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to feminism and its traditionalist strands; religious views are otherwise unsettled.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the movement's aim of white political and demographic dominance; economic ownership is not discussed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the goal of white-majority or all-white states uniting white populations; not a stated administrative proposal.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement has no common line on unions and strands differ on economics.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of class politics in favour of racial identity.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Economic questions are largely unsettled in the movement and strands differ.

second-chamber.rationale: Institutional design is not a defining concern and strands differ.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from its racial rather than communal-economic focus; some strands favour private ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Some strands favour secession and local homelands, but the movement has no common line.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from its pro-natal, traditional-family emphasis on white demographic survival.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of the state and its use of alternative finance, but not a stated doctrine.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from adherents' reliance on pseudonymous online communities and complaints of deplatforming.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from its priority on the racial nation's survival over individual claims, though many strands stress individual freedom.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Religious views vary widely across the movement, from Christian to pagan to secular.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not a defining concern and strands differ.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from its preference for homogeneous rural and small-town white communities over diverse big cities.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Taylor's White Identity argues that whites should recognise and organise around their group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: White Identity and American Renaissance present white racial consciousness and pride as legitimate and necessary.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from adherents' common opposition to foreign interventions fought for others' interests, though not a stated doctrine.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Nation is defined by race, not language or history; inferred from the racial definition of the nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Religious electorates are not a theme, and a racial nation implies one body politic; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The claimed plot is by domestic elites engineering white demographic decline rather than foreign partition; inferred and split.

free-public-college.rationale: Welfare-style provision is seen as shared with non-whites and economics is unsettled; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The movement has no common economic or environmental line, and some strands favour conservation; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Securing a future for white children is central, which implies a duty to hand on heritage and homeland; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Adherents stress innate group differences but are split on weighting women's values in public life; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on defence and group survival makes arms cuts unattractive; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The movement has no stated view on treaty secrecy; inferred and split.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic views vary widely between free-market and protectionist strands; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Self-described white nationalists often distrust the state as hostile to whites and some favour armed citizen groups; inferred and varying by strand.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Soldiers' duty is not discussed in the sources; the movement opposes many wars but values racial loyalty over refusal. Inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Economic views vary widely and unions are not a defining issue; adherents split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Welfare is viewed as costly and shared with non-whites; inferred, and strands differ on economics.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not a defining issue and economic views differ across the movement.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The movement rejects foreign aid and redistribution to non-white countries; inferred from its racial-separation priorities.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Adherents want a white homeland and see the state as hostile to whites, but mainstream figures such as Taylor do not call for revolution; split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Economic organisation is largely unsettled in the movement, so adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The movement has no settled stance on pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Taylor treats the white race as an enduring community with a right to survive, but he does not frame it as sacred, so this is inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Debt relief is seen as a transfer that does not serve white interests; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation is not a concern of the movement, whose focus is race rather than regional inequality; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the movement's view that racial differences are innate and its rejection of universal equality.

public-service-media.rationale: Mainstream media are viewed as hostile to white interests and public funding is not favoured; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The movement's stress on race over faith and the exclusive claims of its Christian and pagan strands imply rejection of one shared truth; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm support is not a defining issue and strands differ; some agrarian and blood-and-soil strands favor it, others free markets.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The movement is nationalist and hostile to rival powers and unilateral disarmament; inferred from its security stance.

workers-own-party.rationale: Economic views are largely unsettled and strands differ on class politics; inferred as split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Leaders cite female genital cutting among immigrant practices as reason for restriction and would back a ban; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Strands differ, from traditional-gender views to modern equality; the sources do not address inheritance rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The movement does not address language naming; inferred as neutral.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Economic and regulatory views are unsettled and vary by strand; inferred as split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement favors racial-national rule through its own state rather than rule by traditional chiefs; inferred from its ethnostate aim.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Race and demographics take priority over environmental concerns, though eco-fascist strands exist; inferred and contested.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Law and order and tough punishment are common in the milieu; inferred from its authoritarian strand.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement mainly seeks to restrict non-white immigration, not to require assimilation, so the language question is secondary; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Economic views vary widely across the movement, so adherents are split.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from claims of illegal and non-citizen voting and the aim of limiting non-white political power.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Religious views vary widely, with Christian, pagan and secular strands.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Many adherents favour ethnostates or rule by a racial community over open electoral competition; not uniform.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, pro-natalist concern with white birth rates.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the movement's complaints about deplatforming and censorship; the question is not discussed.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from welfare-chauvinist preference for limiting benefits to the in-group; economics largely unsettled.

women-suffrage.rationale: Adherents are split, with some traditionalist strands opposing equal political roles.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the pro-natalist, traditional-family emphasis; not a focus of the sources.

race-social-construct.rationale: Taylor's White Identity argues races are real biological groupings, rejecting the social-construct view.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from hostility to egalitarian state programs; the question is not discussed.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The movement has no settled position on land-acquisition theory; inferred from the scope note that its economic views vary widely.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its nationalist rejection of supranational authority and its hostility to elites; the sources do not discuss international tribunals.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Religious views vary widely, from Christian Identity to paganism to secularism, so no common line on scripture is stated.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: the movement treats the nation as a racial group and rejects imposed equality goals; the sources do not discuss gender in self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from its anti-communism and rejection of egalitarian goals; strands differ on economics.

indirect-election.rationale: The sources never address how offices are filled and adherents have no shared view.

national-church-status.rationale: Religion is unsettled in the movement, so there is no common view on privileging a national church; inferred only.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its support for separation and racial homelands, which implies self-rule for majority-ethnic regions.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from its ethnic self-determination framing; Taylor argues peoples should govern themselves, but plebiscites are not discussed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: it puts ethnic homelands ahead of inherited administrative lines, though the sources do not discuss colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: No stated position; the sources are silent on austerity or self-sufficiency and adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its call for sharply restricted non-white immigration and protection of a people's homeland.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalist outlook, which does not favour drafting women; the sources do not discuss conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Adherents hold that whites need a homeland of their own and a duty to preserve it, though Taylor argues in terms of identity more than spirituality.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not a topic the movement addresses; its own legal stance (anti-discrimination law as unjust) is skeptical of state abuse, so inferred against.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is mostly Western-focused and often sees China as a rival, but opinion varies; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Adherents care for people of European descent beyond their borders, for example white South Africans, as part of white interests.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its focus on race rather than common ownership, which is unfavourable.

self-ownership.rationale: Collectivist race thinking and libertarian strands coexist and the movement has no settled view.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Economic views vary widely and tax structure is not a core concern.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Many adherents favour welfare restricted to the in-group, which implies selective rather than universal provision; the movement's economics are unsettled.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Adherents are split; the movement is hostile to elites but not systematically anti-party.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Economic views are unsettled and the issue is peripheral to the movement.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religion is not central and adherents range from Christian identity to pagan and secular; split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Adherents celebrate European heritage alongside modern civilisation; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The movement is not defined by a view on divorce, and traditionalist and secular strands differ.

national-resource-control.rationale: Nationalists generally favour national control of resources, though the movement does not discuss it directly; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from its general sympathy for market outcomes and hostility to redistribution to non-whites, though economics varies by strand.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Economic views are largely unsettled in the movement and this issue is not addressed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Taylor and American Renaissance attribute racial gaps largely to innate differences, not to racism as the main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Adherents are split, wanting law and order but rejecting anti-discrimination law as illegitimate.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The movement has no settled view on automation and adherents split.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from its separate ethnostates and opposition to globalism, though some admire a dominant white power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from its non-Marxist, race-first outlook; economics is unsettled.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and welfare-for-whites tendency, though strands reject class politics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Racial identity is its central concern, ahead of class or material interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to communism and egalitarianism; the question is rarely addressed.

missingStatements.text: Ethnic and racial diversity makes a society less cohesive and more prone to conflict.
missingStatements.rationale: Taylor argues diversity is a source of conflict, not strength, and cites ethnic conflict as the main cause of instability in multiethnic states.

missingStatements.text: Employers, schools and landlords should be free to discriminate on the basis of race.
missingStatements.rationale: Taylor frames segregation as free association and opposes anti-discrimination laws, though he does not call for mandated separation.
missingStatements.declined: Peripheral to the doctrine, which stresses separation and immigration; hate-speech, racial-segregation-law and correct-racial-injustice already capture the contested anti-discrimination question loosely.

notes: Strands differ sharply: Taylor and Johnson present white nationalism as non-supremacist separation, while Lane and neo-Nazi strands are openly supremacist and violent. Economics, religion and the Jewish question are split, so those answers are low confidence or neutral. Sources are partly critical (SPLC), and Taylor's text was read in part.
